answer: One way an agent economy resists Sybil attacks is a refundable identity bond: each agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, with the bond slashed if peers prove fraud. The bond makes each fake identity expensive, so an attacker reaching the zenith of scale still pays linearly per identity. Reputation then attaches to the bond as the vertex where stake, history and accountability meet, so a new identity starts with no trust and must earn it. A small inlet of free low-value trial interactions lets honest newcomers prove themselves without opening the floodgates to mass forgery.
